title: My vocation is love
hook: Thérèse finds her place in the Church's heart
carry: love in the heart of the church

segments.voice: Yesterday, the elevator: Thérèse, too small for the stairs, found her lift in the arms of Jesus. Your line was carried up. What did you let yourself be carried through? Day one thousand two hundred eighty-one.

What do you want to be? Thérèse's answer was: everything. Inside the walls of a small Carmel in Normandy, she writes that she feels drawn to every calling at once. She wants to be a warrior for the Church. A priest. An apostle traveling the world. A teacher. A martyr. Each desire pulls in a different direction, and she can't live any of them from a convent cell. The wanting itself, she says, becomes a kind of suffering. So she does what she did with the staircase. She opens her Bible. Today is what she found there.
screen: `WHAT DO YOU WANT TO BE?` → `EVERYTHING, AT ONCE.` → `SHE OPENS HER BIBLE.`

segments.voice: She turns to Saint Paul's first letter to the Corinthians, chapters twelve and thirteen. Paul describes the Church as one body with many members. Some are apostles, some prophets, some teachers, and he asks whether all are apostles. Not everyone can be everything. Thérèse reads the list, and she doesn't find herself in it. She keeps reading. Paul goes on to a more excellent way, and the chapter about charity, ending, "the greatest of these is charity." And something opens. If the Church is a body, she reasons, it must have a heart, and that heart burns with love. Love is what moves every other member. Without it, apostles would stop preaching and martyrs would refuse to shed their blood. Love holds every vocation inside it. Then she writes the line in her own French: ma vocation, c'est l'amour. My vocation is love. In the heart of the Church, her mother, she will be love. And so she'll be everything she dreamed of, without leaving the cell. Then, because this is Thérèse, she brings it down to size. She can't do great deeds, so she'll do small ones: a smile, a kind word, a sacrifice no one sees, given like flowers scattered before a king. That's the whole connection to yesterday. The little way isn't small in its aim. It aims at the heart of everything, one small act at a time.
screen: `THE CHURCH IS A BODY.` · `SHE ISN'T IN PAUL'S LIST.` · `A BODY MUST HAVE A HEART.` · `SMALL ACTS, SCATTERED LIKE FLOWERS.` · then, large: `MY VOCATION IS LOVE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: do one thing with love. Settle, and breathe. Think about the next ordinary task waiting for you: dishes, an email, a drive, a diaper. Decide now to do that one thing with love, as a gift to someone, without announcing it. If you pray, you can offer it ahead of time, the way Thérèse offered her small acts. If you don't, just picture yourself doing it gently, fully, and well. Stay with that picture until the bell. The bell holds the time.

My vocation is love. Thérèse's discovery: in the body of the Church, she will be the heart. This week ran from Teresa's friendship prayer to John's counsels, the desert, and Thérèse's elevator and heart. Today's word.
Your line: love in the heart of the church. Today, pick one small, hidden act and do it with love, for someone who won't know it was you. Day one thousand two hundred eighty-one.

howItsDone: Catholics who love Thérèse read this passage of Story of a Soul and try to offer small, hidden acts of love in ordinary life, her way of being love in the heart of the Church.
